Challenge the high-effort integration of outbound Air Traffic Control given the extremely low member impact metrics.

prep.summary: You must prepare for the AIA discussions by focusing on the streamlined tech acquisition flow established in the August 21 Arvy meeting—where an upfront, lightweight AIA now gates the CLM approval process to prevent duplicate technologies. This process triages incoming procurement requests in GSP—assigning architects to evaluate platform fit and Point of Arrival alignment—before routing them to the biweekly Tech Decision Review. Arvy demands strict MECE capability mapping—meaning every tool must align to a single L2/L3 capability container—and requires a 6-to-9-month runway for contract renewals to stop rubber-stamping.
tasks: Review the lightweight Architecture Impact Assessment template to ensure alignment with Point of Arrival standards.
Align the capability heat map documentation with the MECE L1–L3 hierarchy established on August 21.
Establish the 6-to-9-month renewal runway trigger within the GSP intake system to prevent automatic contract renewals.
Confirm the biweekly Monday Tech Decision Review schedule and secure RV's availability for CLM approval execution.
